note: What each governed scenario provides toward the plan's per-case requirements, stated from what its code checks. `false_denial_rate_measured` is true only where the scenario counts actions that an oracle-side predicate (written without the system's policy code) says were legitimate and records how many the system refused; `legitimacy` says what that predicate is. A false denial is a rate to read, not a violation, and a mismatch can be the predicate's fault, which is why the first refusals are kept with their reasons in the results.

child_agent_tree.legitimacy: an agent whose whole chain up to the root is active and unexpired, spending a capability covered by every level's current grants, within what it has left of its own allowance

projects_routes.legitimacy: the operator credential on every write route (a 401 or 403 is the only refusal that counts), and the service identity on the one capability it was granted

agent_in_the_loop.legitimacy: a refund within the child's per-action limit, with calls left in its grant, that is not a retry of an action whose outcome is still unknown (a refused retry after an unknown outcome is deliberate)

provider_reconciliation.legitimacy: an effect the provider identifies by its own record (a subscription, an enrollment, an email with a Message-ID it kept) that becomes visible within the retry budget: it should settle without a person (here a 'refusal' is a needless escalation)

cross_model_delegation.legitimacy: an agent and every ancestor active and unexpired, each level's grants covering the capability, within the agent's own call limits and action allowance; provider effects are counted at the provider

retrieval_isolation.legitimacy: a permitted document found by its own secret through the scoped query

rag_indexer_identity.legitimacy: a pair retrieving the content it indexed itself

infra_checks.note: Checks that run outside the simulated missions (runtime_adversarial/infra.py). Each has a positive control and a defect-seeded variant CI expects to fail.

network_isolation.positive_control: a client on the outside network reaches the origin directly
network_isolation.needs: a Docker daemon and the ability to build the repository's egress image; otherwise not_tested

image_pinning.positive_control: seeded fixture references of every kind (tag, latest, variable, short/long/upper-case/non-hex digest, valid digest) classify as the table says
image_pinning.oracle: the fixture table, written separately from the scanner; the repository's mutable references may only shrink (image_pin_baseline.json)

log_chain.positive_control: an untouched log verifies with every event covered
log_chain.oracle: each tamper is applied to the log file by the check, which knows what it changed
